patch_description: This approach estimates where traffic would accumulate if demand were spread across direct and two-hop routes, then uses that estimate to shape the QUBO. Direct-link rewards reflect demand and endpoint activity; two-hop rewards are allocated across candidate intermediates according to route suitability and transit pressure. A separate, modest overlap penalty discourages choosing same-endpoint links with redundant traffic profiles, encouraging more balanced access to the network. This differs from relying primarily on direct demand and uniformly budgeted two-hop rewards, while keeping the quadratic term count below the limit.
